before.title: Type-A Hecke Specht modules are in the same block iff their labels have the same e-core
before.statement: Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$, and let $S^{\lambda}$ be the type-A Hecke Specht module of this page in the Dipper-James convention ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) for $\lambda\vdash n$. Then for all partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ the modules $S^{\lambda}$ and $S^{\mu}$ lie in the same block of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Equivalently the blocks of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ of size at most $n$ with $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. (For $e=\infty$ the Hecke algebra is semisimple and each partition is its own core, so the statement is the trivial block decomposition.)

before.title: Weight-one block decomposition pattern
before.statement: Let $e\ge2$, let $\gamma$ be an $e$-core of $m$, and put $n=m+e$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). There are exactly $e$ partitions $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$ of $n$ with $e$-core $\gamma$; list them in dominance order, $\lambda_1\rhd\lambda_2\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$. In the source's (Murphy/dual-Specht) normalisation the Weyl modules and simple modules of this block satisfy $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$ and $[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]$ for $1\le k<e$, so the decomposition matrix is the $e\times e$ bidiagonal matrix with rows and columns $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$; and exactly $\lambda_1$ is not $e$-restricted while $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_e$ are. Under the Schur functor ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]) the corresponding Murphy Specht classes are $[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_{k+1}}_{\mathrm M}]$ for $2\le k<e$ and $[S^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]$, with $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$; conjugating partitions and dualising ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]) gives the corresponding decomposition matrix for the page's Dipper-James Specht modules in $e$-regular labels.
before.strategy: The abacus of [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]] shows that the partitions of $n=m+e$ with $e$-core $\gamma$ are obtained from $\gamma$ by moving one bead up one row on one runner, so there are exactly $e$ of them; ordered by dominance they are $\lambda_1\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$, with $\lambda_e$ the one whose bead has the lowest target position and $\lambda_1$ the one obtained by adjoining all $e$ boxes to the first row. For each $k$ the Jantzen sum formula of [[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]] evaluates in this weight-one configuration to $\sum_{i>0}[W^{\lambda_k}_F(i)]\sim\sum_{j>k}(-1)^{j-k+1}[W^{\lambda_j}_F]$, because the only nonzero hook valuations are the consecutive ones; the resulting triangular system, with the simple modules detected through [[lem-virtual-weyl-combinations-detect-q-schur-block-separation]] and the block classification, has the unique solution $[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]$ for $k<e$ and $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$. The $e$-restricted pattern follows from $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$, which is exactly the non-$e$-restricted vanishing of the cell head, together with $F(W^{\lambda_1})=F(L^{\lambda_2})$ and the Schur-functor dictionary; the Dipper-James translation is the conjugation/duality dictionary of the Specht-module definition. This is Mathas, Proposition 5.38 with its printed Jantzen computation, printed pp. 61-63; the numeric pattern is worked out again in this pair's examples companion. No choice principle is used.
